meaning.en: This śloka praises Lalitā as Unapproachable by sinners, stops evil customs, Free from all faults, Omniscient, shows intense compassion, and neither equal nor superior. Rather than presenting unrelated titles, the verse gathers these qualities into one vision of the Divine Mother.

Rather than presenting unrelated titles, the verse gathers these qualities into one vision of the Divine Mother.

meaning.kn: ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವು ಲಲಿತೆಯನ್ನು bhānumaṇḍalamadhyasthā, bhairavī, bhagamālinī, padmāsanā, bhagavatī, padmanābhasahodarī ಎಂಬ ನಾಮಗಳಿಂದ ಸ್ತುತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಈ ನಾಮಗಳು ಪ್ರತ್ಯೇಕ ವಿಶೇಷಣಗಳಲ್ಲ; ಒಂದೇ ದಿವ್ಯಮಾತೆಯ ಪರಸ್ಪರಪೂರಕ ಸ್ವರೂಪಗಳನ್ನು ಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿ ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

meaning.en: This śloka praises Lalitā as bestows Her grace immediately, Witness to the whole universe, no other witness, Accompanied by the deities of the six angAs (heart, head, hair, eyes, armor and weapons), and Fully endowed with the six good qualities (prosperity, valor, dispassion, fame, wealth and wisdom). Rather than presenting unrelated titles, the verse gathers these qualities into one vision of the Divine Mother.
meaning.kn: ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವು ಲಲಿತೆಯನ್ನು sadyaḥprasādinī, viśvasākṣiṇī, sākṣivarjitā, ṣaḍaṅgadevatāyuktā, ṣāḍguṇyaparipūritā ಎಂಬ ನಾಮಗಳಿಂದ ಸ್ತುತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಈ ನಾಮಗಳು ಪ್ರತ್ಯೇಕ ವಿಶೇಷಣಗಳಲ್ಲ; ಒಂದೇ ದಿವ್ಯಮಾತೆಯ ಪರಸ್ಪರಪೂರಕ ಸ್ವರೂಪಗಳನ್ನು ಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿ ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

Taken together, the names in this verse develop grace, devotion and compassion, Her all-pervading universal nature, a distinct aspect of Her divine nature. Taken together, the names in this verse develop a distinct aspect of Her divine nature, the inseparability of Śiva and Śakti, sacred knowledge and mantra. Each epithet contributes a particular facet, so the movement of the śloka is cumulative: Lalitā is contemplated not only through a single attribute but as the Reality in which these dimensions meet.

The deeper Śrīvidyā reading is that form, power, knowledge and transcendence are not separate compartments of the Goddess. They are different ways the one Śakti becomes knowable to the devotee. The verse therefore invites a unified contemplation of Lalitā—as the personal Mother who can be loved and worshipped, and as the consciousness that ultimately exceeds every name used to praise Her.
